title: How to Prepare a Character or Mascot Design Project
h1: How to prepare a character or mascot design project
description: What to prepare before commissioning a character or mascot: personality, audience, uses, style references, turnaround sheets, expressions, rights and files.
intro: A well-designed character can become the face of a brand, a book series or a game. Mascots and characters are used for years, in many poses and formats, so they need more planning than a single illustration. Buyers who only describe a cute animal and leave the rest to the artist often end up with a design that works in one picture but not across a website, animation and merchandise. This article explains what to prepare before you commission a character.

faq.a: A reference showing the character from several angles, with colors and key details, so others can draw it consistently.

faq.q: How many expressions do I need?
faq.a: Enough for your planned uses. Many brands start with five to ten expressions and poses.
It depends on use. 2D suits illustration and simple animation; 3D suits games, AR and product-style visuals.
Agree in writing. For mascots and series characters, aim for full rights or broad exclusive rights.

faq.q: Can I use AI tools for a character?
faq.a: Consider consistency, rights and originality. Discuss openly with the artist before starting.
